summary: ssm-kernel-explorer written. Controls: modulus slider r (0.5-0.999, nonlinear: 0.9-0.999 takes half the travel), angle slider theta (0-pi in steps of pi/64, fraction labels), input-signal select (5 options), T slider (50-400 step 10), continuous-time toggle (pole alpha, omega, step Delta replace r/theta), selective-step toggle (w, c, alpha; theta greyed, retention panel). Default r=0.95, theta=pi/8, impulse at t=5, T=120: kernel period 16, half-life 13.51, K_0..K_5 = 1, 0.878, 0.638, 0.328, 0, -0.296, dots on the recurrence line. Checked widget vs independent Python (labpy) in 6 discrete states, 4 continuous states and 5 selective states (incl. noisy sine via a Python mulberry32 replica, w=0, extremes): lambda, |lambda|, angle, half-life, period, bbar, K_0..K_5, final output, peak |y|, Delta_t and a_t ranges all agree to display rounding; recurrence-vs-convolution max difference 0 to 1e-13 (1.4e-13 at r=0.999, T=400).
changes: Selective mode with w=0 shows the constant-step kernel a^k b and the convolution dots again; with w!=0 the kernel panel shows 'no fixed kernel' text
Readout adds K_0..K_5, final output and peak |y| so numbers can be checked
Canvases get taller aspect at narrow width
issues: widget-test.mjs reports changedOutput=false for the select and toggles because it restores them before comparing; verified by probe that they change the output
theta and omega sliders are integer multiples of pi/64 (slider position 0..64), the r slider position is nonlinear so probe values for it are slider positions
Selective view takes precedence when both toggles are on (continuous toggle disabled)
Selective alpha is a separate slider with default 1 so a_t = exp(-Delta_t) as in the text; max diff for noisy-sine tests is 5e-15
